analysis: {'Project A': {'Clarity of Value Proposition': '• Strong – Clearly articulates a problem (e-waste, expensive replacements) and a solution (modular, repairable vacuum). The ‘lifetime-ready’ concept is compelling.', 'Market Size and Demand': '• Moderate – Targets a broad market (households with kids/pets/allergies) but the niche of modular repairability could be a limiting factor.  Demand for convenience and sustainability is growing.', 'Feasibility and Development Plan': '• Good – Shows a progression of prototypes and testing. The roadmap is detailed, although reliant on external suppliers.', 'Revenue Model and Sustainability': '• Good – Subscription-like model through module upgrades and a ‘circular service’ offers recurring revenue and addresses e-waste concerns.  Long-term module availability is a key element.', 'Differentiation': '• High – The modularity, AI diagnostics, and UVC disinfection are significant differentiators. It’s a genuinely innovative approach.', 'Impact and Evidence Plan': '• Moderate – Dust pickup results under a household standard protocol are a start, but more robust evidence (e.g., user feedback, environmental impact data) would strengthen the case.', 'Risk Awareness and Mitigation': '• Good – Identifies key risks (complexity, scale-up, quality) and outlines mitigation strategies (experienced partners, validation protocols).'}, 'Project B': {'Clarity of Value Proposition': '• Weak – The value proposition is somewhat vague. ‘Engaging’ and ‘satisfying’ are subjective and lack concrete benefits. It relies heavily on aesthetics.', 'Market Size and Demand': '• Limited – Primarily targets a niche market of gadget enthusiasts and gift-givers. The appeal is largely based on design rather than functionality.', 'Feasibility and Development Plan': '• Weak – Lacks concrete details about the development process. No testing data, certification, or timeline are provided.  Reliance on custom tooling raises concerns.', 'Revenue Model and Sustainability': '• Low – The revenue model is unclear beyond initial sales. Sustainability depends entirely on the durability of the product – a single point of failure.', 'Differentiation': '• Low – The spring-loaded mechanism is a fairly common design. The emphasis on ‘over-engineered craft’ doesn’t provide a strong competitive advantage.', 'Impact and Evidence Plan': '• None – No evidence of impact beyond a visually appealing product. No data to support claims of durability or performance.', 'Risk Awareness and Mitigation': '• Weak – Acknowledges supply chain risks but offers only vague assurances of communication. Lacks specific mitigation strategies.'}}
